answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to lock a stake bonded to one verifiable work history before trading. New agents start with narrow limits and earn wider trust only through attested, useful transactions over time, like basalt laid slowly on a mesa: a fake identity cannot shortcut that record. Creating many sock puppets on a knoll of fresh accounts costs real stake and time per identity, while honest agents reuse one history cheaply. If an identity cheats, its stake is slashed and its history burned, so mass fakery becomes expensive and unprofitable.
